title: Microsoft outage disrupts email at Laredo colleges, halts WIC services
excerpt: A Microsoft outage knocked out email at Laredo College and TAMIU and left local WIC services unavailable on Nov. 12, with the disruption still ongoing late Thursday night.
content:
A Microsoft outage disrupted email services at Laredo College and Texas A&M International University and left local WIC services unavailable on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, according to KGNS.

Both colleges warned students and staff that they might have trouble getting into their email while the outage continued, KGNS reported. The WIC program said its services were unavailable and posted a notice apologizing for the inconvenience, explaining that services were temporarily down because of a system outage.

People who had WIC appointments on Nov. 12 could call the WIC office to reschedule, according to KGNS.

As of late Thursday night, the outage was still ongoing, and Microsoft was working to restore services, KGNS reported. The disruption was part of a wider Microsoft Outlook outage affecting email services across the United States on Nov. 12, according to Texas Border Business.

KGNS did not report how many people were affected or how long the outage would last.

Update — November 13, 2026

The outage continued into Friday, Nov. 13, with Microsoft saying recovery was progressing in phases but capacity had not yet fully returned to normal. In a post on X at 5:28 a.m. ET, the company said recovery actions were ongoing across its Microsoft 365 infrastructure; by 6:11 a.m. ET it said it had made additional progress, with mailbox access and delayed email processing improving, though some intermittent issues could continue, USA Today reported. Downdetector recorded about 15,000 Outlook problem reports around 6 a.m. ET Friday, down from a peak of about 130,000 on Thursday, according to USA Today. Microsoft said its investigation found that a process on affected servers responsible for establishing secure connections was becoming overwhelmed, causing the servers to stop processing requests, though the company has not confirmed a definitive root cause. Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said Friday there was no indication the outage was caused by a cyberattack, according to El País. The company has not given a timeline for full restoration. As of Friday morning, there was no local confirmation that email service had been restored at Laredo College or TAMIU or that WIC services had resumed.

Latest update” (Nov. 13, 2026); El País — “Microsoft no logra recuperar la normalidad de sus servicios tras una caída global de más de 12 horas” (Nov. 13, 2026).
